en: I praise Gaṇeśa—the dwarf, yet exceedingly stout; with the face of a lordly elephant, pot-bellied and beautiful;
the Lord of Obstacles, whose temples are swarming with bees greedy for the scent of ichor.

I bow to Gaṇapati, the son of the Daughter of the Mountain, who rends his enemies with the uprooting of their tusks, who creates the beauty of vermilion, and who bestows both spiritual accomplishments and the fulfillment of desires. || 1 ||
Heramba is the supreme deity who brings about the accomplishment of all tasks; grant me the abundance of happiness, endowed with good fortune and beauty. (2)
I bow to the son of Gaṅgā, who has a single tusk, a massive body, a protruding belly, and the face of an elephant; he is the bestower of all spiritual accomplishments. || 3 ||
I bow to that noble Gaṇanātha, the sinless one, who is a forest fire to the drought of poverty;

who shakes away all impurities with the trunk of his proboscis; and who is a boat for crossing the ocean of saṃsāra—to him, the best of lords, by bowing to whom tens of millions of gods attain supreme perfection.
His body was as red as vermilion, and he was drenched by streams of ichor flowing forth. || 4 ||
Bearing a pair of frontal globes that rival the two lofty hemispheres of the universe, delighting with his broad ear-flaps that challenge the wings of the enemy of the serpent’s foe,
the Lord— Śambhu’s offspring— possesses hands that grow to rival the body of the lord of serpents.
Victorious is the elephant-faced Lord of the three worlds, whose form is a marvel to the three realms! || 5 ||
Gaṇapati, Heramba, Vidhṇarāja, and Vināyaka—the son of the Goddess, possessed of great splendor, great strength, and great prowess. || 6 ||
Large-bellied and large-bodied, with a single tusk and the face of an elephant;
clad in white garments, greatly radiant, three-eyed, he is the leader of the Gaṇas. || 7 ||
Holding a rosary and a tooth in his right hand,
and grasping an axe and a bowl of sweetmeats in his left hand.
The god delights in various flowers and is anointed with various fragrant unguents;
his body has a serpent for a sacred thread, and he is the destroyer of various kinds of obstacles. || 9 ||
I bow to him who is worshipped by gods, asuras, humans, siddhas, and gandharvas; who removes obstacles for the three worlds; and who is mounted upon a rat. || 10 ||
Sumukha, Ekadanta, Kapila, Gajakarṇaka, Lambodara, Vikaṭa, Vināyaka, and Vināyarāja. || 11 ||
Dhūmraketu, the leader of the Gaṇas, Bhālacandra, Gajānana, Vakratuṇḍa, Śūrpakarṇa, Heramba, and the elder brother of Skanda. || 12 ||
Whoever should recite or even hear these sixteen names at the commencement of learning, at a wedding, at entering [a house], or likewise at departing; || 13 ||
In battle and in times of distress, no obstacle arises for him.
Salutations to the Lord of the Gaṇas, the axe that cuts down the creeping vine of obstacles. || 14 ||
The Śrīgaṇeśastotra is completed.
